chunks.arabic_text: أَحْمَدُ بْنُ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ سَعِيدِ بْنِ حَمَّادِ بْنِ سَعِيدِ بْنِ مِهْرَانَ، يَكْنَى أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ.

translations.en: Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd ibn Ḥammād ibn Saʿīd ibn Mihrān, known by the kunya Abū Jaʿfar.

chunks.arabic_text: رَوَى عَنْ أَكْثَرِ رِجَالِ أَبِيهِ، وَقَالُوا: "سَائِرُهُمْ إِلَّا حَمَّادَ بْنِ عِيسَى". وَقَالَ الْقُمِّيُّونَ: كَانَ غَالِيًا. وَحَدِيثُهُ - فِيمَا رَأَيْتُهُ - سَالِمٌ. وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ. وَهُوَ الْمُلَقَّبُ "دَنْدَنُ".

translations.en: He narrated from most of the men of his father, and they said: 'All of them except for Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā.' And the Qummis said: 'He was a ghālī (exaggerator).' And his ḥadīth - in what I have seen - is sound (sālim). And God knows best. And he is the one nicknamed 'Dandān'.

en.summary: This entry from al-Ghadā'irī’s *Kitāb al-Ḥadāʾiq* (or *al-Duʿafāʾ*) highlights Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥusayn’s complex scholarly standing, noting his reliance on his father’s network while explicitly excluding Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, a key figure in the transition from Kufan to Baghdadi hadith transmission. The designation of 'ghālī' by the Qummis reflects the theological debates regarding the Imams' divinity or authority, yet the narrator's overall reliability (*salām*) suggests his hadiths remain valid despite potential theological nuances. His laqab 'Dandān' serves as a distinctive identifier within the chain of narrators, preserving his memory in the biographical dictionaries.
en.seo_question: Who is Ahmad ibn al-Husayn Dandan and what is his status in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.غَالِيًا: ghālī (exaggerator, one who exaggerates in the virtues or status of the Imams)
key_terms.سَالِمٌ: sālim (sound, free from major defects or irregularities)
key_terms.كُنْيَة: kunya (a teknonym or nickname, usually derived from one's eldest son)
